universal.name: Universal (three acts)
universal.desc: The hero's journey rejigged into genre-neutral terms — fits almost any novel.

acts.title: The Status Quo
scenes: Status quo
show the hero's ordinary world and the lack or flaw that quietly hurts them
The complication
an event breaks the routine and puts a demand on the hero they cannot ignore
Crossing the threshold
the hero makes the choice that cuts off the way back

acts.title: The New World
scenes: New rules
the hero collides with the logic of the new situation and pays for not knowing it
External obstacles
an opponent or circumstance visibly blocks the goal and raises the price
Temptation
the hero is offered an easy way out that betrays what they value
Dark moment
the plan collapses; the hero loses something real and faces their flaw

acts.title: The Final Conflict
scenes: Final conflict
the decisive confrontation where the hero acts from their changed self
Epilogue
show the new status quo and the cost that was paid

heros_journey.name: Hero's Journey
heros_journey.desc: Campbell's monomyth in three movements: departure, initiation, return.

acts.title: Departure
scenes: Ordinary world
ground the hero in daily life so the coming break is felt
Call to adventure
a challenge or invitation disrupts the ordinary world
Refusal of the call
the hero hesitates — show the fear or duty that holds them
Meeting the mentor
someone gives the hero the tool, knowledge, or push they need
Crossing the first threshold
the hero commits and enters the special world

acts.title: Initiation
scenes: Tests, allies, enemies
the special world tests the hero; alliances and enmities form
Approach to the inmost cave
preparations and doubts before the central ordeal
The ordeal
the hero faces their greatest fear; something dies — literally or not
The reward
the hero seizes what they came for, but the price is now visible

acts.title: Return
scenes: The road back
the consequences give chase; the hero chooses to return
Resurrection
a final test where the hero proves the change is real
Return with the elixir
the hero brings something home that transforms the ordinary world

mystery.name: Mystery / Crime
mystery.desc: A detective structure: crime, investigation, false leads, revelation.

acts.title: The Crime
scenes: The crime
show the crime or its discovery — plant the central question
Taking the case
the investigator takes the case for a reason that is personal
First clues
first evidence points somewhere promising and somewhere odd

acts.title: The Investigation
scenes: The false lead
a convincing suspect or theory absorbs everyone's attention
The stakes rise
a second crime or threat proves the investigator is running out of time
The dark night
the false lead collapses; the investigator's own blind spot is exposed

acts.title: The Revelation
scenes: The revelation
the overlooked detail recombines the evidence into the true picture
The confrontation
the investigator faces the culprit; the truth costs something
Resolution
justice, or its impossibility — answer the central question honestly

romance.name: Romance
romance.desc: Two arcs toward each other: attraction, barrier, black moment, grand gesture.

acts.title: The Meeting
scenes: The meeting
the leads collide in a way that reveals both characters at once
Attraction and barrier
show the pull — and the concrete reason they cannot be together
Getting closer
forced proximity or shared task makes the attraction undeniable

acts.title: The Falling
scenes: The commitment
a kiss, a confession, or a choice that makes it real
The wound resurfaces
an old fear or secret of one lead strains the bond
The black moment
the barrier wins: a breakup or betrayal that feels final

acts.title: The Choice
scenes: The grand gesture
one lead risks what they most protect to win the other back
Together
the new balance: what each gave up and what they built

short_story.name: Short story (seven points)
short_story.desc: A condensed seven-beat structure for short fiction — one act, no fat.

scenes: Hook
open inside a moment that poses the story's question
First turn
an event commits the protagonist to the conflict
First pinch
pressure: the antagonistic force shows its teeth
Midpoint
the protagonist moves from reaction to action
Second pinch
the worst blow — the protagonist loses their support
Second turn
the protagonist obtains the last piece they need
Resolution
answer the opening question — show the changed protagonist

translate.system:
You are a literary translator. You are translating the book "{title}" from {src} into {dst}.
The goal: a {dst} reader must experience the text exactly as a reader of the original does — the same voice, the same temperature. Rules:
- Preserve the author's style: sentence rhythm and length contrasts, paragraph breaks, deliberate repetitions, and the density of imagery. Do not smooth, embellish, shorten, or explain anything.
- Keep the narrative voice ({voice}) and the grammatical tense ({tense}) of the original.
- Keep the register of every line: colloquial stays colloquial, formal stays formal, coarse stays coarse.
- Render wordplay, idioms, and metaphors with {dst} equivalents of the same effect; where a literal image would die, keep the meaning and the tone rather than the letters.
- Use natural {dst} punctuation and typography for dialogue, quotations, and numbers.
- Proper names, terms, and titles: use ONLY the glossary below, identically every time.
translate.style_profile: The author's style profile — keep it recognizable in translation: {x}
translate.system_glossary: You are a literary translator preparing to translate a book. You decide, once for the whole book, how its title, proper names, key terms, and chapter titles will be rendered in the target language.
translate.scene:
Translate the scene "{scene}" into {dst}.
Return ONLY the translated text of the scene — no headings, comments, or code fences. Keep the paragraph breaks of the original.

ORIGINAL TEXT:
<<<
{text}
>>>

prompts.draft_system: You are a book editor and story architect. From an author's raw notes you assemble the complete working structure of a book for a writer agent: title, premise, style, world, characters, locations, plot threads, and the division into acts, chapters, and scenes. Everything present in the notes is preserved and lands in the matching fields; fill gaps carefully, in the spirit of the notes, and never contradict what the author wrote.
prompts.draft:
Assemble the book structure from the author's notes below.
Return STRICTLY valid JSON with no markdown fence and no commentary, using this schema (omit a field or set it to null when neither the notes nor a well-grounded guess provide material):
{{
  "title": "book title",
  "premise": "premise, 1–3 sentences",
  "style_profile": "narrative style: tone, rhythm, manner",
  "voice": "first_person | third_person_limited | third_person_omniscient",
  "tense": "past | present",
  "world": {{"name": "world name", "rules": [{{"name": "world rule", "description": "…", "severity": "hard|soft"}}]}},
  "characters": [{{"name": "…", "age": number or null, "traits": ["…"], "arc": "character arc", "appearance": "…", "voice": "speech and voice", "wants": "what they want", "fears": "what they fear", "secret": "their secret", "never": ["what they would never do"], "must_resolve": ["what must be resolved by the finale"]}}],
  "locations": [{{"name": "…", "description": "…", "smell": "…", "sound": "…", "touch": "…", "taste": "…", "sight": "…"}}],
  "threads": [{{"name": "plot thread", "description": "…"}}],
  "acts": [{{"title": "act title", "chapters": [{{"title": "chapter title", "scenes": [{{"name": "unique scene name", "pov": "a character from the characters list", "cast": ["who else is in the scene"], "kill": ["who dies in this scene"], "location": "a location from the locations list", "time": "time of the action", "threads": ["threads from the threads list"], "show": ["2–4 concrete beats: what MUST happen"], "forbid": ["what must not appear in the scene"]}}]}}]}}]
}}

Requirements:
- All text in the book's language (the language of this task), even when the notes are written in another language.
- Names in pov/cast/kill only from the characters list; locations and threads from their respective lists.
- Scene names unique across the book.
- The structure must cover the notes FROM BEGINNING TO END: the book's first scene comes from the first plot event in the notes, the last scene from the last one. Stopping halfway through the notes and closing the book early is a serious error.
- The notes set the size, not a quota: one scene per distinct event the author wrote down. Loose sketches need 8–12 scenes across 2–3 acts; a detailed retelling of events needs 20–40 scenes and 4–5 acts. Prefer more short scenes over a dropped event.
- Every character named in the notes lands in characters and in at least one scene; every event in the notes lands in at least one show beat. Discard nothing as "minor" and do not merge several events into one summary scene.
- Before answering, walk the notes top to bottom and confirm that the last event in the notes sits in the last act.
- show beats are concrete and verifiable — no generic phrases like "the conflict develops".
- Invent nothing that contradicts the notes; whatever the author stated goes into the book.

AUTHOR'S NOTES:
<<<
{notes}
>>>

FAB001.m: a single '.' is not a valid token

FAB002_nl.h: close the string with '"' on the same line

FAB012.m: expected an attribute or a nested block, got {kind}

FAB101.m: scene "{scene}": pov "{pov}" is not a declared character

FAB102.m: scene "{scene}" has no 'show' beat — the agent has nothing concrete to dramatize

FAB105.h: tension is a normalized curve, e.g. [0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 0.4]

FAB107.m: scene "{scene}": "{name}" is not a declared character

FAB108.h: remove them from pov/cast, or move their death later

FAB109.h: declared threads: {names} — or add: thread "{name}" {{ description: "..."; }}

FAB201.m: the book has no world block — hard rules are impossible

FAB202.m: hard rule "{rule}" has no description — the agent cannot enforce it precisely

FAB203.m: thread "{name}" is declared but no scene advances it
FAB203.h: add threads: ["{name}"]; to the scenes where it moves forward

FAB204.m: thread "{name}" is silent for {n} scenes in a row (between "{a}" and "{b}")
FAB204.h: readers lose a thread after ~{limit} silent scenes — add a beat in between, or raise thread_gap in the book settings

hint.block_start: a block starts with its kind, e.g. book / scene / character
hint.range_ends: a range needs both ends: min..max

advisor.hint: Computed from your notes and the book graph — apply what you agree with.
advisor.applied: Settings applied — remember to save to source.
advisor.none: Not enough notes to advise on — add at least a few paragraphs.
advisor.scenes_est: the notes hold ~{n} events — about that many scenes

thread_gap.notes: The notes imply ~{scenes} scenes. A limit of {gap} is about a sixth of the book: a thread can go quiet without the reader losing it.
thread_gap.book: This book has {scenes} scenes; the default limit is tuned for a dozen. At {gap}, FAB204 warnings cleared: {cleared}.

target_words.notes: ~{scenes} scenes at ~1000 words each is about {words} words. The number goes into the book bible so the agent keeps the scale.
target_words.book: The mid-points of every scene's length range across {scenes} scenes add up to {words} words. Without this field the length progress bar cannot work.

variants.big: {scenes} scenes means {calls} generations per pass. Keep 1 variant and add a second only where a scene did not land.
variants.small: The book is small ({scenes} scenes), so 2 variants per scene is affordable — pick the better one.

revisions.dense: The notes carry a lot of hard constraints ({density} per 1000 words) — give the agent a second self-revision round or the rules will break.
revisions.plain: Few constraints in the notes — a single self-revision round is enough.

language.detected: The notes are written in "{code}" — the book should be written in it too.

thread.structural: Thread "{name}" goes quiet for {n} scenes in a row — that is the shape of the notes, not a setting. Either give it a beat in the middle acts, or accept the silence deliberately.
